reason:
Independent Claude review of the claude-only provider policy change (scripts/nightshift-provider-policy.py, tests/test-provider-policy.sh, plus the wiring diff in scripts/nightshift-agent.sh, nightshift-route.sh, nightshift-factory.sh, nightshift-behavior-proof.py, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, docs/BEHAVIOR-PROOF.md, commands/nightshift-adversarial.md). Traced every managed launch boundary by hand (no execution — the sandbox declined to approve running test-provider-policy.sh/test-agent-dispatch.sh/test-factory-auth.sh, so those remain unverified stub tests per the no-stub-as-proof instruction, not evidence I'm relying on).

Checked and found consistent with the documented contract:
- Precedence/composition: mode() in nightshift-provider-policy.py:14-41 unions NIGHTSHIFT_PROVIDER_POLICY, NIGHTSHIFT_HOME, project dir, git toplevel, and (via --git-common-dir) the primary checkout for a linked worktree, and returns 'claude-only' if present anywhere in that set — matches the documented "restrictions compose, cannot be relaxed" rule, and covers worktree inheritance (mode():21-28).
- Invalid/forbidden-provider handling fails closed: any value outside ('standard','claude-only') raises ValueError (line 39-40); nightshift-agent.sh:177 and nightshift-factory.sh:288 both `|| exit`/`fail` on nonzero from the policy script; select_route() raises when claude-only has no configured Claude route (line 58) or a non-string/empty model (line 60), and main() catches ValueError/OSError/KeyError/TypeError/SubprocessError and returns exit 64 (lines 88-90) — no silent fallback to a forbidden provider anywhere in the paths I traced.
- Automatic local routing (gear 0 for low-risk nightshift-code-fact-extractor) is correctly overridden under claude-only: nightshift-route.sh:21-22 always re-runs the selected gear-0 route through select_route, which substitutes a real claude gear (haiku at gear 1) and relabels gear→1 (nightshift-provider-policy.py:52-56).
- Default-policy compatibility: with policy=='standard' and no --adversarial, select_route() returns the initial route unchanged; the adversarial cross-provider swap path (line 61-64) reproduces the pre-change bash logic in nightshift-agent.sh/nightshift-behavior-proof.py byte-for-byte in intent, so non-opted-in projects see no behavior change.
- Factory CLI precedence (nightshift-factory.sh:277-341): --provider-policy cannot relax an inherited claude-only env value (280-283); an explicit --provider codex/local under claude-only is caught by the line-338 check, which runs after the model-alias substitution block (299-317) that is the only other place PROVIDER can change post-resolution, so there's no ordering gap that lets a forbidden provider slip through model-alias resolution.
- Fresh same-provider review / no session resume: nightshift-agent.sh's claude launch branch now always adds --no-session-persistence (line ~229); challenge_admission/challenge_proof in nightshift-behavior-proof.py require 'review_independence:fresh-session' in rules_fired when policy is claude-only (line ~1524) and that tag is only emitted by nightshift-agent.sh when policy==claude-only AND --adversarial was set (the jq at line ~313), so a same-provider approval without the adversarial fresh-session flag cannot pass.
- Approval reuse across a policy change is blocked by challenge_policy_current() (nightshift-behavior-proof.py, ~line 1409-1417), applied both to the "not authoritative" check (~838) and the "challenge_stale" check (~904), comparing the policy recorded on the receipt against a live re-resolution of mode() — an approval minted under one policy cannot be reused for finalize/seal validation under a different one.
- Digest/identity/provenance binding: challenge_proof re-derives provider_policy(proof.project) at validation time and blocks with challenge_provenance_changed if it, the routing file's sha256, or the reviewer provider drifted from what challenge_admission recorded (~lines 1531-1533) — closes the TOCTOU window between admission and validation.

No confirmed or plausible blocking defect was found in this pass across the listed boundaries; the only items noted (redundant re-application of select_route() when routing through nightshift-route.sh then nightshift-agent.sh again, and non-cached importlib reloads of the policy module per call) are idempotent/inefficiency-only, not correctness bugs, so they are not reported as findings. Per the task's own caveat, this review does not claim OS/network isolation guarantees beyond Nightshift's managed launch boundary, matching what docs/CONFIGURATION.md states explicitly.

claims.claim: select_route() forces claude-only routing and fails closed with no permitted Claude route
mode() composes project/global/worktree/env policy restrictively and rejects invalid values
factory CLI cannot relax an inherited claude-only restriction and rejects an explicit non-claude provider
claude launches under nightshift-agent.sh always disable session persistence and reviews require the fresh-session rule tag under claude-only
challenge_policy_current() blocks reuse of a challenge approval after the provider policy changes
challenge_proof revalidates routing digest and provider policy at finalize time to prevent provenance drift between admission and validation
